chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And your garments purify,' he said: 'Roll them up.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'purify your garments' in Surah Al-Muddaththir according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a practical exegesis of Surah Al-Muddaththir, linking the spiritual command to purify one's garments with the physical act of rolling them up (takhbiyah) to avoid soiling them with dust. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on combining ritual purity (taharah) with practical hygiene and modesty, reflecting the Prophet's tradition of keeping garments above the ankles to prevent arrogance and dirt. The hadith serves as a foundational text for the fiqh of dress, illustrating how literal actions can fulfill broader spiritual obligations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High, and [74:4] And your garments do purify. Heasws said: ‘Roll-up (i.e. keep them clean, not let them drag on the ground)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

About the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, . . and cleanse your clothes’, [74:4] abu £ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It means lift up (cut short) your clothes (instead of dragging them on the ground).”’
